problem:
Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2t+{t}^{3},\,{p}_{2}(t)=3-t-3{t}^{3}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

examples.problem:
Consider the polynomials $p_1(t)$ and $p_2(t),$ given by

$$
p_1(t)=3+2t, \qquad
	p_2(t)=-t+t^2.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $\mathcal{B}=\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ are ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068026/assets/3274a690fa59f7d7368fcbe54004eab244c9845e20bf03ffce1e9fa25bbaf4bc.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Any vector in $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068026/assets/170acd827e8b97471869159c5d9af88b0e4324b25ca1b42ec652011ece6a5174.png)

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =4\cdot (3+2t)+(-3)\cdot (-t+{t}^{2}) \\  & =12+8t+3t-3{t}^{2} \\  & =12+11t-3{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
